joins-and-grain.title: Why a joined order amount appears twice
joins-and-grain.summary: Order 101 has Amount 100 and two payments, 60 and 40. This is a row-matching map: both payment rows are valid, but joined rows are no longer one row per order.

nodes.label: Order 101 · Amount 100
nodes.description: One order row at order grain.

nodes.label: Joined row · 101 / 100 / 60
nodes.description: The order fields are repeated alongside the first payment.

nodes.label: Joined row · 101 / 100 / 40
nodes.description: The same order fields are repeated alongside the second payment.

nodes.label: SUM(order amount) = 200; SUM(payment) = 100
nodes.description: The payment sum is meaningful here; the order sum double counts the original 100.

steps.title: Inspect both grains
steps.explanation: One order matches two payments on OrderId. OrderId is not unique in the payment input.

steps.title: Build the first match
steps.explanation: SQL attaches the complete order amount 100 to payment 60; it does not allocate the order amount.

steps.title: Build the second match
steps.explanation: Payment 40 produces another row carrying order amount 100. This is expected join expansion, not an accidental duplicate payment.

steps.title: Check totals at the output grain
steps.explanation: 100 + 100 exaggerates sales. If the required output is one row per order, first aggregate payments by OrderId, then join that one-row-per-order result.

transactions-isolation.title: A deliberate failure rolls back the work copy
transactions-isolation.summary: Follow the lesson’s single-session #LNAtomicWork example with @@TRANCOUNT = 0 at entry. It demonstrates rollback, not how other sessions observe concurrent changes.

nodes.label: Before BEGIN TRAN · Amount 100
nodes.description: The temporary work copy contains order 101 with Amount 100.

nodes.label: Inside transaction · Amount 999
nodes.description: UPDATE changes order 101 in the work copy, but the transaction has not committed.

nodes.label: THROW 51001
nodes.description: The simulated failure transfers control to CATCH; the following COMMIT is not reached.

nodes.label: CATCH and transaction-state check
nodes.description: If XACT_STATE() is nonzero, ROLLBACK undoes remaining transactional changes.

nodes.label: Final SELECT · Amount 100
nodes.description: The final verification sees the original amount. The demo reports the error instead of rethrowing so this SELECT can run.

steps.title: Start from the work copy
steps.explanation: The precondition rejects an existing outer transaction. Order 101 starts at 100 in the copied temporary table.

steps.title: Make an uncommitted change
steps.explanation: The current transaction updates Amount to 999. This is not yet a successful committed unit of work.

steps.title: Take the failure path
steps.explanation: THROW prevents execution from reaching COMMIT. CATCH inspects XACT_STATE and rolls back if a transaction remains.

steps.title: Verify the original value
steps.explanation: The final SELECT returns 100, not 999. The demonstration catches the error for teaching; production code should usually propagate failure.
